items.title: Most of the 300 vehicles reported stolen in Peel last month taken from Mississauga
items.summary: There have been 300 vehicles reported stolen to Peel Regional Police over the last 31 days, with more than half of those pilfered vehicles being taken from owners in Mississauga. The numbers come from the Peel police crime map, which tracks reported incidents of crime like assaults, drug trafficking and break-ins, and shows 300 a combined 300 vehicle thefts reported in both Mississauga and Brampton between Aug. 5 and Sept. 5. Of those 300 reported incidents, 178 happened in Mississauga. Another 118 occurred in Brampton, while the remaining four vehicle thefts were not given a location on the map. The map also identified “hot spots” in both cities, pointing to Toronto Pearson International Airport and the Square One shopping centre in Mississauga, and the area of Bovaird Drive and Highway 410 as locations with a higher number of reported vehicle thefts. And while Mississauga tallied the highest number of stolen vehicles reported, Brampton saw more violent crimes, according to the data. The map shows there were a combined 320 assaults reported in Mississauga and Brampton between Aug. 5 and Sept. 5, with 190 or more than 59 per cent of incidents occurring in Brampton. Another 127 (more than 39 per cent) of reported assaults happened in Mississauga, with the remaining three assaults not mapped. There were also a combined 24 robberies reported across both cities. Six of those incidents were reported in Mississauga, while the remaining 18 occurred in Brampton, according to the data.

items.title: Bert Fleming Park Redesign Heads Back to Mississauga Council Next Week
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga city councillors will revisit revised plans next week to enlarge and redesign Bert Fleming Park in the city's west end. The outlet reports the park, located along The Credit Woodlands north of Dundas Street West near Mississauga Road, is being transformed through the Credit Woodlands Integrated Road Project. INsauga reports the project will expand the park by about half an acre and add new pedestrian crossings and sidewalks to better connect it to the surrounding neighbourhood. According to the outlet, city officials describe the goal as turning Bert Fleming Park into a neighbourhood hub where residents can gather, play and connect with nature. INsauga reports the revised design follows a community open house and survey held earlier this year, with staff adjusting the plan to prioritize the facilities and amenities that residents said they supported most.

items.title: City Now Expects Lakeview Village to Land Closer to 12,000 Units, Below Provincial Cap
items.summary: According to The Pointer, the City of Mississauga has confirmed that the massive Lakeview Village waterfront development is now projected to include closer to 12,000 residential units, down from the 16,000-unit maximum allowed under a 2023 provincial zoning order. The outlet reports the project sits on 177 acres along the eastern lakeshore where the former coal-fired Lakeview power plant once stood, and had been planned for years through collaboration between residents, developers, council members and city staff. The Pointer reports the Ontario government issued a Minister's Zoning Order in May 2023 at the request of the development consortium, doubling the maximum allowed units from 8,000 to 16,000 and leaving many involved in the original planning process feeling betrayed. According to the outlet, the city's communications team said it is now processing several initial phase site plan approval applications from the ownership consortium that include a mix of building types, including townhomes. The Pointer reports the province's 16,000-unit figure remains the maximum threshold for residential density, even though the city expects the actual build to come in lower.

items.title: Peel Public Health Shuts Down Popular Mississauga Dosa Restaurant Over Food Storage Violations
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Public Health has shut down Swagruhas, a South Indian vegetarian restaurant at 2970 Drew Road in Mississauga known for its sweet and savoury dosas, after the location failed a health inspection. The outlet reports the restaurant was inspected and closed on Thursday, September 3. INsauga reports the inspection report cited the restaurant for not properly storing food to prevent contamination and for failing to take adequate measures to prevent pests, among other violations. According to the outlet, the restaurant will remain closed until it passes a follow-up inspection. INsauga reports this is the only failed inspection on file for the restaurant, which has an inspection history dating back to October 2024, and that Peel Public Health issues a red card, forcing closure, only when significant health risks are found.

items.title: Peel Police Board Seeks Public Input as It Drafts New Youth Engagement Plan
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Peel Police Service Board is developing a new Youth Engagement Plan aimed at strengthening relationships between police and young people across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. The outlet reports the board wants input from students, parents, educators, community organizations and other residents as it shapes the plan. INsauga reports Sumeeta Kohli, chair of the board's Governance and Human Rights Committee, said meaningful youth engagement begins with meaningful community engagement. According to the outlet, the plan is still being developed and public feedback is expected to play an important role in the process. INsauga reports the initiative reflects a broader trend among police services across the country to build trust with young people before interactions become focused on enforcement.

items.title: Mississauga Locks In $401.4 Million in Transit Funding by Committing to Development Charge Cuts Through 2029
items.summary: According to Connect CRE Canada, Mississauga has secured up to $401.4 million in federal and Ontario infrastructure funding after committing to maintain steep cuts to residential development charges through March 31, 2029. The outlet reports the city reduced development charges by 50 per cent beginning January 29, 2025, and will eliminate them entirely for rental units with one bedroom plus den, two bedrooms, or three bedrooms. Connect CRE Canada reports the funding could support a zero-emission transit maintenance and storage facility on city-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue, including bus storage and a maintenance garage. According to the outlet, a second allocation could advance downtown transit infrastructure, including a Transit Mobility Hub, transitway connections, bus platforms, and pedestrian and bike facilities. Connect CRE Canada reports the funding remains subject to a Canada-Ontario Build Communities Strong Fund agreement and other approvals, with participating municipalities required to contribute at least 10 per cent of project costs. According to the outlet, the city estimates the measures could help unlock 90,000 new homes.

Mississauga August Home Sales Slip 13 Per Cent as Days on Market Stretch to 54, Zoocasa Finds
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's housing market cooled in August, with home sales falling 13 per cent month-over-month to 435 transactions, based on Zoocasa's analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The outlet reports average days on market lengthened to 54 from 47 in July, as the pace of sales slowed. INsauga reports Zoocasa said the decline in new listings outpaced the drop in active inventory, which helped limit how much supply was available to buyers. According to the outlet, the average selling price for a detached home was $1,275,221 in August, slightly higher than July's $1,256,800 but below the $1,362,799 average recorded in August 2025. INsauga reports the average price for a semi-detached home was $879,494, down from $891,613 in July and $973,755 a year earlier.

items.title: 22-Unit Affordable Rental Building Breaks Ground in Mississauga's Meadowvale Area
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, construction has begun on a new affordable rental housing project in the city's Meadowvale area. The outlet reports the four-storey building, located at the northwest corner of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Britannia Road, will include 22 units. Mississauga.com reports 18 of those units will be subsidized through affordable housing incentive programs run by Peel Region and the City of Mississauga. According to the outlet, project owner Safwat Boulos said the development was first proposed in 2022 as a 20-unit project and is expected to be ready for occupancy before the end of 2027. Mississauga.com reports the building will offer a mix of one-bedroom plus den, two-bedroom plus den, and three-bedroom plus den units, with the project having secured both regional and municipal funding.

items.title: Toronto Pearson to Offer First Nonstop Flights to Norway Under Air Canada's 2027 Expansion
items.summary: According to INsauga, Air Canada has announced three new international routes launching from Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga in the summer of 2027, including its first nonstop flights to Norway. The outlet reports the new destinations are Oslo, Shannon in Ireland, and Nice in France, with Oslo becoming Air Canada's third Scandinavian route alongside existing service to Stockholm and Copenhagen. INsauga reports the Oslo flights will fly aboard the airline's new Airbus A321XLR aircraft, which features a premium Signature cabin with lie-flat seats. According to the outlet, Toronto Pearson president and CEO Deborah Flint said the new routes strengthen links to global markets and give passengers more choice. INsauga reports the airline is also adding a seasonal Toronto to London-Heathrow day-tripper service, daily flights to Shanghai, and a new year-round route to Guatemala City starting this December.

items.title: Province of Ontario's Name Traces Directly Back to Lake Ontario, Column Explains
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent column traces the centuries-old history behind the name Lake Ontario, noting that the Province of Ontario itself takes its name directly from the lake. The outlet writes that the lake's shores have been home to Indigenous peoples for thousands of years before European colonization. Modern Mississauga Media reports that after 1608 the region was part of New France's Pays d'en Haut, or Upper Country. According to the outlet, Britain reorganized the area as the Province of Quebec following the 1763 Treaty of Paris, which ended French colonial rule after the fall of New France. Modern Mississauga Media reports the Constitutional Act of 1791 later split that territory into Upper Canada, now Ontario, and Lower Canada, now Quebec. The column was prompted partly by recent attention in the United States over proposals to rename the lake, which the outlet says has only reinforced pride in the name's Canadian identity.
